integrity_notes.finding: Every 'divisible by both X and Y' diagram table in sets 1-2 had the correct answer as the only all-yes row, visible on the worksheet (not just the key) -- answerable by pattern-matching rather than real reasoning. Affected: set 1 #27, set 2 #13, set 2 #35 (all answered correctly). Fixed in set 3 and confirmed absent from all other live worksheets (checked all 5).

Real-test (a x b)-over-c estimation items always use a slash (e.g. '(51 x 743) / 25'), never a division sign -- checked all 9 real examples in the library. Set 2's #3/#33 (already taken) and set 3's original #3/#26 used ÷. Fixed in set 3 (now /); can't change set 2. Doesn't change the math or the gap finding, just a minor notation mismatch worth knowing about.

Same bug class as the 2026-10-08 divisibility leak: set 2 #6 and set 3's original #26 both had a 'Number / Round to' diagram table printed directly on the question sheet (not just the key), handing over the entire estimation step before she'd attempted it. Set 2 #6 was already taken and answered correctly (consistent with the leak making it trivial) -- can't fix retroactively, documented here. Set 3 #26 fixed: diagram removed, numbers swapped to (46 x 227) / 23. Caught by the parent noticing the table I'd described as a teaching aid was actually already live on the question sheet, not just something I was proposing.

Opposite problem from the usual leaks: set 3 #37 (Split Line Segments) under-specified rather than over-specified. Its number-line diagram showed only letter labels 'Q' and 'P' with no numeric scale anywhere -- no origin, no per-tick value -- while the answer key's own explanation assumed 'Q=10, P=30, 5 per tick,' information that was never actually rendered on the page. The problem was unsolvable as administered; already taken and graded wrong (consistent with there being no way to derive the answer from what was shown). Found while building the post-test review and tracing why her wrong pick (60) didn't match any described trap. First fix (2026-10-11) labeled every tick from 0 through P, but that doesn't match real ISEE style, so it was superseded same day: cross-checked against an actual official-test screenshot of an equivalent midpoint problem, which labels only the two visible line endpoints (never the lettered points) and stops the line short of the answer's position. Final diagram: arrowed line from 0 to 35 (only those two endpoints numbered), Q and P shown as bare letters, R (=50) off the visible line entirely. CORRECTION, same day: #23 was NOT actually unaffected as originally claimed here -- see the next entry.

#23 (the other Split Line Segments problem) also didn't match the real-test format, caught later the same session: it stated the point values directly in the question text ('A is at 14 and C is at 50') instead of showing them on a diagram for her to read off, which is how every real 'X is the midpoint of Y and Z' problem in the library presents this content. Fixed on the live worksheet: question now reads 'Use the number line...' with a proper diagram (line from 2 to 56, only endpoints 2/56 labeled, A and C shown as bare letters), matching the same convention used for #37's fix above.

Informal retest: after #23 and #37 were both fixed on the live worksheet, the parent had Hannah redo both problems directly (not inside a new timed set). She answered both correctly, each in under 1.5 minutes. This is consistent with the two format bugs being the actual cause of the original misses rather than a genuine midpoint-vs-distance gap -- but isn't fully conclusive, since she was redoing problems she'd just missed rather than fresh ones, so some of the speed/accuracy could reflect having already worked through the method once. Treating Split Line Segments as provisionally resolved (bug-caused, not a gap) unless a *new* problem on this topic in a future set produces another miss, which would reopen it. Tracker priority downgraded from needs-retest to low; raw wrong/graded counts on set 3 left unchanged since they reflect what actually happened.
